title: The Contract Act, 1872
text: Section 27. Agreement in restraint of trade void: Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void. Exception 1.—Saving of agreement not to carry on business of which good-will is sold: One who sells the good-will of a business may agree with the buyer to refrain from carrying on a similar business, within specified local limits, so long as the buyer, or any person deriving title to the good-will from him, carries on a like business therein: Provided that such limits appear to the Court reasonable, regard being had to the nature of the business.

title: The Contract Act, 1872
text: Section 74. Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for: When a contract has been broken, if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of such breach, or if the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused thereby, to receive from the party who has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or, as the case may be, the penalty stipulated for.

title: The Contract Act, 1872
text: Section 23. What considerations and objects are lawful, and what not: The consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless— it is forbidden by law; or is of such a nature that, if permitted, it would defeat the provisions of any law; or is fraudulent; or involves or implies injury to the person or property of another; or the Court regards it as immoral, or opposed to public policy. In each of these cases, the consideration or object of an agreement is said to be unlawful. Every agreement of which the object or consideration is unlawful is void.

title: The Contract Act, 1872
text: Section 56. Agreement to do impossible act: An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. Contract to do act afterwards becoming impossible or unlawful: A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful.

title: The Competition Act, 2012
text: Section 15. Prohibition of anti-competitive agreements: (1) No enterprise or association of enterprises shall enter into any agreement in respect of production, supply, distribution, storage, acquisition or control of goods or provision of services, which causes or is likely to cause an adverse effect on competition. (2) Any agreement entered into in contravention of subsection (1) shall be void. (3) Any agreement entered into amongst enterprises or persons at different stages or levels of the production chain in different markets, in respect of production, supply, distribution, storage, sale or price of, or trade in goods or provision of services, including tie-in arrangement, exclusive supply agreement, exclusive distribution agreement, refusal to deal, and resale price maintenance, shall be an agreement in contravention of sub-section (1) if such agreement causes or is likely to cause an adverse effect on competition.

title: The Competition Act, 2012
text: Section 16. Abuse of dominant position prohibited: (1) No enterprise shall abuse its dominant position. (2) There shall be an abuse of dominant position if an enterprise directly or indirectly imposes unfair or discriminatory conditions in purchase or sale of goods or service, or prices in purchase or sale (including predatory price); limits or restricts production of goods or provision of services or market therefor; indulges in practice or practices resulting in denial of market access in any manner; or makes conclusion of contracts subject to acceptance by other parties of supplementary obligations.

title: The Arbitration Act, 2001
text: Section 10. Power of court to stay judicial proceedings: Where a party to an arbitration agreement brings an action before a court against another party to the agreement in respect of any matter agreed to be referred to arbitration, any party to the arbitration agreement may, not later than when submitting his first statement on the substance of the dispute, apply to the court to stay the legal proceedings and refer the parties to arbitration.

title: The Arbitration Act, 2001
text: Section 46. Enforcement of foreign arbitral awards: (1) Any foreign arbitral award made in pursuance of an agreement to which the New York Convention applies shall be recognized as binding on the persons as between whom it was made, and may accordingly be relied on by any of those persons by way of defense, set-off or otherwise in any legal proceedings in Bangladesh.
